questions.q: How does Oracle's CASE expression decide which result to return?
options: It evaluates WHEN conditions in order and returns the result of the first one that is true
It averages the results of every WHEN condition
It always returns the result of the last WHEN condition
It returns all matching WHEN results as a list
questions.explain: CASE evaluates WHEN conditions top to bottom and stops at the first one that evaluates to true.

questions.q: What are the standard five AP/AR aging buckets built in this lesson?
options: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly
Current, 1-30 Days, 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days, 90+ Days
Open, Closed, Pending, Approved, Rejected
Small, Medium, Large, Extra Large, Jumbo
questions.explain: Current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, and 90+ days overdue is the industry-standard aging bucket structure.

questions.q: Why is it important for the day ranges in a CASE-based aging bucket to be mutually exclusive and gapless?
options: It isn't important — CASE automatically fixes overlapping ranges
Because ELSE is required to be the first condition
Because CASE stops at the first matching WHEN, so overlaps or gaps can silently put a row in the wrong bucket or no bucket
Oracle rejects any CASE expression with more than 3 WHEN clauses
questions.explain: Since CASE returns on the first match, poorly bounded ranges can misclassify rows without raising any error.

questions.q: When grouping by a CASE expression's result, what must you do in the GROUP BY clause?
options: Reference the column alias assigned to the CASE expression
Omit GROUP BY entirely — CASE results group automatically
Use HAVING instead of GROUP BY
Repeat the full CASE expression, exactly as written in SELECT
questions.explain: Oracle groups by the actual expression, not an alias defined in SELECT, so the full CASE expression must be repeated in GROUP BY.

questions.q: What does the ELSE branch of a CASE expression do?
options: It raises an error if no WHEN condition matches
It provides the result returned when none of the WHEN conditions are true
It is evaluated first, before any WHEN condition
It is required syntax with no functional effect
questions.explain: ELSE is the fallback result used only when none of the preceding WHEN conditions evaluated to true.
